 ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR)

This petition is filed by the petitioner/accused No.1 under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita, 20231, with the following prayer:
"The petitioner being accused No-1 in Spl.C.C. No.01/2025 pending before the III Additional District and Sessions Judge Dharwad (Spl. Judge for CBI/ACB/KLA cases) registration on Crime No.251/2022 registered by the 1st respondent Vidyagiri Police for the offences punishable under sections 406, 409, 419, 420, 465, 467, 468,
471, 201, 204, 120B Read With sections 34 and 35 of IPC and Section 7(A), 13(1)(A),
13(2) of PC Act 2013 Hereinafter referred to as the 'BNSS, 2023' NC:
Vasantkumar Alias Sajjan V D S/O ... vs State Of Karnataka on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140086347/
2 2026:KHC-D:3294 HC-KAR in so far as petitioner is concerned and prayed for any other order or direction upon the facts and circumstances of the case in the interest of justice and equity."
2. The allegation against the petitioner/accused No.1 is that he was working as a Special Land Acquisition Officer2 of KIADB at Dharwad.

It is alleged that though compensation amount was granted to land losers during the years 2011-12, 2012-2013 and 2018, but once again the petitioner in collusion with the other accused and with common intention, fraudulently created and fabricated documents with malafide intention to dupe money from the Government.
On the basis of such forged and concocted documents, compensation was allegedly disbursed for second time.
Thus, in this way, the petitioner caused a loss to the State Exchequer of Rs.19,99,55,000/-.

Accordingly, a case was registered against the petitioner/accused No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 201, 204, 120-B read with Sections 34 and 35 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 7(A), 13(1)(A), 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Bill,
20133.

Hereinafter referred to as the 'SLAO' Hereinafter referred to as the 'P.C. Act' NC:
2026:KHC-D:3294 HC-KAR 3.

This is a successive bail petition filed by petitioner/accused No.1.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.1 submitted that the Investigating Officer has now filed charge sheet against the petitioner/accused No.1 and other accused persons, and therefore, the petitioner is no longer required for custodial interrogation.
Furthermore, the petitioner/accused No.1 is in judicial custody since 10.04.2023.

It is further submitted that the offences alleged are primarily triable on the basis of documentary evidence, and hence there is no question of tampering with the evidence or threatening the witnesses.
Therefore, prays to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned High Court Government Pleader submitted that though charge sheet is filed, the Investigating Officer has sought permission to file an additional charge sheet.

It is further submitted that the quantum of siphoning of the State Exchequer amount is a huge one and from the charge sheet it is clearly revealed that the petitioner/accused No.1 has played an active role in conspiracy and in collusion with NC: 2026:KHC-D:3294 HC-KAR the other accused persons.
Therefore, he prays that the petitioner shall not be enlarged on bail.
6. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondents No.1 and 2.
Perused the material available on record.
7. The petitioner is in judicial custody since 10.04.2023 and has attained superannuation.
The petitioner is in custody for nearly three years.
The maximum punishment prescribed for the offences alleged is imprisonment up to ten years.
Thus, the petitioner has undergone almost one-third of the maximum sentence prescribed.
The Investigating Officer has filed the charge sheet.
Considering the offences alleged, the case of the prosecution is primarily based on documentary evidence.

It is pertinent to note that some of the accused have already been granted bail and in respect of certain other accused, the Investigation Officer has filed a 'B' report.

3 8.

Having regard to the aforesaid factors, particularly the period of custody already undergone by the petitioner, the filing of the charge sheet, and the fact that the prosecution case is NC:
2026:KHC-D:3294 HC-KAR mainly based on documentary evidence, hence, the chances of threatening witnesses is remote.
Accordingly, the petitioner is enlarged on bail with the following conditions.

9. Hence I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed.

ii. The petitioner/accused No.1 is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.251/2022 of Vidyagiri P.S., Dharwad, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 419, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 201, 204, 120B read with Sections 34 and 35 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 7(A), 13(1)(A), 13(2) of P.C. Act, pending on the file of III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Dharwad, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- along with one surety for the like sum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3294 HC-KAR b) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Trial Court without prior permission of the Court.
c) The petitioner shall not tamper and threaten the prosecution witnesses in any manner.

d) The petitioner shall mark his attendance before the concerned police station on every Saturday between 11.00 a.m. to 02.00 p.m.
e) The petitioner shall attend the Court regularly during the trial without fail.
If not attend for consecutive two times, it entails cancellation of bail.
iii. Violation of any one of the conditions would entitle the prosecution to seek for cancellation of bail.
